name: static-entities

args.prompt:
Use the attached first-eight board ONLY as our own material, lighting and contour reference. Replace the board with the NEW complete layout below; do not preserve or repeat the original eight objects. Create a clean production sprite atlas of SIXTEEN DISTINCT ORIGINAL CLOCKWORK ART RESOURCES. These are standalone static semantic sprites, NOT animation frames. The game will move, fade, rotate, or place them using its existing presentation logic.

Match the established material family: richly modeled tarnished warm brass rims and rivets, cool blue-grey steel recesses, small bright teal lenses or energy details, crisp fine pixel clusters, and controlled dark outlines. Upper-left warm light; two or three broad value planes; quiet texture. Distinct silhouettes and useful negative space, not flat vector pictograms or recolored copies.

ONE SQUARE image, requested 1024 by 1024, exactly FOUR equal columns by FOUR equal rows. Sixteen different resources, in the row-major order below. Do not crop the outer canvas. Every subject must fit inside the CENTRAL 60 percent of its own cell width and height. Leave at least 20 percent of EACH cell fully transparent along ALL FOUR sides. This leaves at least 64 percent of each cell's area transparent. No subject touches a cell edge, overlaps a neighbor, or spills a glow into the gutter. Keep every resource independently centered, including ground-based objects inside their safe region.

Use true transparent alpha for all negative space. No text, ID labels, digits, rarity borders, grid lines, background, scenery, floor shadow, painted checkerboard, opaque fog, or enormous glow. Do not repeat the same design to imply animation.

Objects:
Row 1, column 1: ONE broad-shouldered bell guardian with a heavy brass breastplate, two short steel stabilizer arms, and one teal clock core. Squat, broad, and clearly armored; no army or group. Distinct from the small patrol drone.
Row 1, column 2: ONE lightly built temporary patrol drone. Show open assembly ribs, an exposed split gear, and one small teal lens. Its incomplete mechanical body remains coherent, distinct from a closed armored drone.
Row 1, column 3: ONE grey steel bell attendant at evolution ZERO: compact core body, bare side hinges, and one dangling brass pendulum. No added rank armor. Keep its body size and central anchor identical to the next two designs.
Row 1, column 4: The SAME grey bell attendant at evolution ONE: add one small upper armor shell and one visible rank notch. Preserve its core, pendulum, body size, pose, and central anchor; do not zoom in.
Row 2, column 1: The SAME grey bell attendant at evolution TWO: add two layered upper armor plates and two visible rank notches with restrained copper trim. Preserve the same core, pendulum, size, pose, and anchor; no giant upgrade.
Row 2, column 2: ONE compact pear-shaped electric urn with two handles, a dark brass cage, one sharp cyan lightning thread inside, and a small jagged top electrode. A recognizable flying vessel, not an explosion.
Row 2, column 3: ONE low flat copper needle-mine base with three unequal silver needle tips and one small cyan trigger lens. It must look planted on its base, not like a floating circular object.
Row 2, column 4: Three angular teal crystal spikes, one tall and two small, rooted in a tiny broken brass fragment. Clear triangular silhouette, luminous facets rather than a large glow cloud.
Row 3, column 1: ONE thin crescent steel shield embracing a tiny teal lens, with a small brass hinge. Strong open protective curve and a large transparent middle; no opaque bubble.
Row 3, column 2: A compact copper trigger plate releasing a short angular crown of flame: two curling amber tongues and a small teal core, with sparse chips and transparent gaps. This is a stationary burst accent, NOT a thrown bomb.
Row 3, column 3: A broken electric urn neck releasing two angular cyan lightning forks and sparse brass bell chips. A clear empty center; distinct from the orange flame burst.
Row 3, column 4: Three narrow silver needle shards fan upward from a low copper base, with tiny teal roots. Sharp, concise, and transparent between the needles; no round grenade cloud.
Row 4, column 1: A thin broken brass cog arc with one heavy off-center pendulum tail. Unequal clock-tooth breaks and a fully transparent interior; avoid a perfect vector circle.
Row 4, column 2: Three unequal clock ticks spring outward around a compact asymmetric shock crest. Emphasize the third tick with a teal core and a few brass chips. No digit or text.
Row 4, column 3: Two broken copper relay contacts face each other across a jagged diamond-shaped pressure star. Small teal electric core; a distinctive mechanical relay burst, not a circle or flame.
Row 4, column 4: One narrow sweeping trail made from three separated crescent blade segments with tiny stepped clockwork notches. Motion flows from left behind toward the right. Keep transparent gaps between the three blades.

admission: Independent reviewer final_review explicitly permitted ONLY four remaining64 icon boards and selected two static16resource boards after realUI/world/frame-sequence golden. New output remains unverified.
new_animation_claim: Two static boards are 32 single-frame resources animated by original runtime age/transforms/fade, not 32 handdrawn animation sets.
